title: Trigonometric Identities
seo_title: Trigonometric Identities Worksheet: Pythagorean, Reciprocal, Even-Odd | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on trigonometric identities: the Pythagorean identity, reciprocal, quotient, even-odd and cofunction identities, and simplifying expressions. 100 questions.
key_sub: Rewrite in sine and cosine, then use the identity. Take the sign from the quadrant.
body_html:
How it works

  • Pythagorean identities: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, 1 + cot² θ = csc² θ.
  • Reciprocal and quotient: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.
  • Even-odd: cos(−θ) = cos θ, but sin(−θ) = −sin θ and tan(−θ) = −tan θ. Cofunction: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ.
  • To simplify, rewrite everything in sine and cosine, then factor and use sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.
  • When you take a square root, choose the sign from the quadrant.
Example

If sin θ = 13 and θ is in Quadrant II, find cos θ.

cos² θ = 1 − 19 = 89

cos θ = ±2√23; cosine is negative in Quadrant II

Answer: −2√23

Example

Simplify sec θ − sin θ tan θ.

= 1/cos θ − sin² θ/cos θ

= (1 − sin² θ)/cos θ = cos² θ/cos θ

Answer: cos θ

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the ± when taking a square root, or choosing the wrong sign for the quadrant.
  • Writing 1 + tan² θ = csc² θ. Tangent goes with secant.
  • Cancelling terms across a sum, such as (1 − cos² θ)/cos θ = 1 − cos θ.
  • Treating sin(−θ) as sin θ. Only cosine and secant are even.

faq.a: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every angle θ. Dividing it by cos²θ or sin²θ gives 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.

faq.q: How do you simplify a trigonometric expression?
faq.a: Rewrite every function in terms of sine and cosine, combine fractions, factor, and use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

faq.q: How do you know whether the answer is positive or negative?
faq.a: Use the quadrant: sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, cosine in I and IV, and tangent in I and III.

faq.q: Which trig functions are even and which are odd?
faq.a: Cosine and secant are even: f(−θ) = f(θ). Sine, tangent, cosecant and cotangent are odd: f(−θ) = −f(θ).

items.q: Simplify sin² θ (1 + cot² θ).
items.e: 1 + cot² θ = csc² θ, and sin² θ · csc² θ = 1. 1.

items.q: Simplify sin⁴ θ − cos⁴ θ.
items.e: Difference of squares: (sin² θ − cos² θ)(sin² θ + cos² θ), and the second factor is 1. sin² θ − cos² θ.

items.q: Simplify cos θ · tan θ.
items.e: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, and cos θ cancels. sin θ.

items.q: Simplify sec θ / tan θ.
items.e: (1/cos θ) · (cos θ/sin θ) = 1/sin θ. csc θ.

items.q: Simplify sec θ · cos θ.
items.e: They are reciprocals. 1.

items.q: Simplify (sec θ − 1)(sec θ + 1).
items.e: sec² θ − 1 = tan² θ. tan² θ.

items.q: Simplify cot θ / csc θ.
items.e: (cos θ/sin θ) · sin θ = cos θ. cos θ.

items.q: Simplify cos θ + sin θ tan θ.
items.e: cos θ + sin² θ/cos θ = (cos² θ + sin² θ)/cos θ = 1/cos θ. sec θ.

items.q: Simplify (1 − cos² θ) / sin θ.
items.e: 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ, and sin² θ / sin θ = sin θ. sin θ.

items.q: Simplify csc θ / cot θ.
items.e: (1/sin θ) · (sin θ/cos θ) = 1/cos θ. sec θ.

items.q: Simplify sin θ + cos θ cot θ.
items.e: sin θ + cos² θ/sin θ = (sin² θ + cos² θ)/sin θ = 1/sin θ. csc θ.

items.q: Simplify cos(−θ) sec θ.
items.e: cos(−θ) = cos θ, and cos θ sec θ = 1. 1.

items.q: Simplify (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ).

items.q: Simplify cos² θ (1 + tan² θ).
items.e: 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and cos² θ · sec² θ = 1. 1.

items.q: Simplify tan θ / sec θ.
items.e: (sin θ/cos θ) · cos θ = sin θ. sin θ.

items.q: Simplify (1 − sin² θ) / cos θ.

items.q: Simplify (sin θ + cos θ)² − 1.
items.e: sin² θ + 2 sin θ cos θ + cos² θ − 1 = 2 sin θ cos θ. 2 sin θ cos θ.

items.q: Simplify tan θ · cot θ.

items.q: Simplify sin θ · cot θ.

items.q: Simplify sin θ csc θ − cos² θ.
items.e: sin θ csc θ = 1, and 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ. sin² θ.

items.q: A point on the unit circle has x-coordinate 513 and is below the x-axis. What is its y-coordinate?
items.e: x² + y² = 1 (cos² + sin² = 1): y² = 1 − 25169 = 144169, so y = −1213.

items.q: If tan θ = 52 and θ is in Quadrant I, find sin θ.
items.e: Use x = 2, y = 5 (signs from Quadrant I). r = √(4 + 25) = √29. Then sin θ = 5√2929.

items.e: cos t = x/2 and sin t = y/6, and cos² t + sin² t = 1, so x²/4 + y²/36 = 1.
